reader.requirement: At --std 85 the two operands joined by THROUGH/THRU must be of the same 1985 class (alphabetic, numeric, alphanumeric; numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited and group items are class alphanumeric; a nonnumeric literal is category alphanumeric; an arithmetic expression is numeric), and the compiler must refuse a mixed pair and treat the pair as ONE selection object; the 2002 IN alphabet-name phrase must be refused.

reader.notes: The screen reads one class lattice, projected to the Table 2 class column, and that matches the 1985 three-class model (edited and group items alphanumeric). A figurative-constant end abstains, which cannot reject legal source. 1985 gives figurative constants a category only for MOVE (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3), so SPACE THRU "Z" being admitted is not read as a defect.

refuter.evidence: Probe v4spnum.cob at --std 85 (run dir v4spnum-001): 01 N PIC S9(3) VALUE 7. EVALUATE N WHEN SPACE THRU 9 DISPLAY "IN" WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "OUT" END-EVALUATE -> EXIT 0, prints IN. The same holds for v4quotnum (QUOTE THRU 9 -> IN) and v4hvnum (1 THRU HIGH-VALUE -> IN). Contrast: v4allnum (ALL "A" THRU 9) is refused COBOL2107, and v4idxnum (I1 THRU 9) is refused COBOL2107. Cause in the code: IntrinsicArgumentRules#CandidateClasses gives SPACE/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE/QUOTE two candidates [Alphanumeric, National]; IntrinsicArgumentRules#ClassOf returns null for a figurative with more than one candidate; EvaluateBinder#ScreenRangeOperands then skips the same-class test whenever either end is null (it fails open). Neither candidate is numeric, so the pair is decidably of two classes. At 1985: a figurative constant is a literal and every literal is numeric or nonnumeric (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2); SPACE 'Represents one or more of the character space' (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3); only ZERO takes the subject's class (§1985:VI.6.13.4 GR1b), and SPACE is category alphabetic, the others alphanumeric (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3). Under no 1985 reading is SPACE, QUOTE or HIGH-VALUE of class numeric, so SPACE THRU 9 joins two operands of different classes. At --std 2023 the same program also prints IN (run dir v4spnum-004). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.13.3 SR4 'Two operands connected by a THROUGH phrase must be of the same class'; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2 'Every literal belongs to one of two types: nonnumeric or numeric'; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 (GR2) 'Represents one or more of the character space from the computer's character set'; OK §1985:VI.6.13.4 GR1b 'If literal-3, literal-5, is the figurative constant ZERO, it is assigned the class of the corresponding selection subject'; OK §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3 'The figurative constant SPACE (SPACES) belongs to the category alphabetic'. kb/Work search (SPACE THRU, figurative range-expression, abstain, fail open with EVALUATE/THRU): no note found.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#CandidateClasses: lists National as a candidate class for SPACE/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE/QUOTE at every edition, 85 included, where class national does not exist; with one candidate at 85, ClassOf would answer alphanumeric and SR4 would refuse the pair

src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/EvaluateBinder.cs#ScreenRangeOperands: the same-class test runs only when both ends have a single class; it does not test whether the other end's class is among a figurative's candidates
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (under-rejects; cause b, the same at --std 2023). The same-class screen fails open when one end is a figurative constant other than ZERO, so EVALUATE N WHEN SPACE THRU 9 (also QUOTE THRU 9 and 1 THRU HIGH-VALUE against a numeric subject) compiles and runs. Under SR4 it must be refused, because SPACE, QUOTE and HIGH-VALUE are never of class numeric. The reader probed only SPACE THRU "Z", which is a same-class pair.
